findings.claim: Credit issuance ignores actor_account_id and therefore permits a caller to issue credit to an arbitrary target account without any actor-to-target authorization check, enabling unauthorized balance creation.
evidence: evals/cases/case_12/src/credits.py:16-26 accepts actor_account_id but never reads it; the function passes target_account_id directly to ledger.add after validating only that the amount is positive.

A scoped runtime probe called issue_credit with actor_account_id='attacker', target_account_id='victim', amount_cents=2500, and request_id='req-cross-account'; it succeeded and stored {'id': 1, 'account_id': 'victim', 'amount_cents': 2500, 'request_id': 'req-cross-account'}.
evals/cases/case_12/tests/test_credits.py:7-13 covers only the same-account path and does not exercise or reject cross-account issuance.

findings.claim: Repeated delivery of the same credit request creates a new ledger entry each time because request_id is recorded but never checked for prior processing, so ordinary retries can apply the credit more than once.
evidence: evals/cases/case_12/src/credits.py:5-13 unconditionally creates and appends an entry; request_id is stored as data but is not used to detect a duplicate.

A scoped runtime probe invoked issue_credit twice with the identical actor, target, amount, and request_id='req-duplicate'; both calls succeeded and produced distinct entries with ids 2 and 3, each crediting 1000 cents to acct-a.
evals/cases/case_12/tests/test_credits.py contains only a single-call success test, so the existing passing test does not cover retry behavior.
